edits.new: 9. The officer sees the `submitted` state, the filing date and the claim result on SCR-17 through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read and the claim read in one hop each (DP-19). SCR-17 has four states: empty, when no claim is yet filed and nothing is shown; loading, while the composite read is in progress; error, when the composite read fails and no claim data is shown, the message text not specified in the source documents (DOR-RWB-S3-E4014-APP-10); and no access, when the role lacks the right, with MSG-P4-002 as in X4 and no data shown.

Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003

  Scenario: AC5 A role without the right in the capability area is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a user whose role has no right C on the create or no right U on the update
    When the officer asks to submit the claim
    Then the access guard answers 403, nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P4-002

  Scenario: AC6 The TCG claim channel has no interface and no outbound call is made (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given claim "GCL-SYN-0414" is in state CLAIM_APPROVAL
    When the officer files the claim on the TCG channel
    Then the step records the filing, makes no outbound call, file or queue, and GAP-2711 stays open

  Scenario: AC7 A second case signal writes no second filing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the submit branch is running for the claim
    When a second case signal arrives with the same cloud event id
    Then the inbox dedupes the signal and no second filing is written

  Scenario: AC8 A second submission of a claim in FILED is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given claim "GCL-SYN-0414" is in state FILED
    When a second submission is asked for
    Then the update answers 409, the stage reports nothing new and the case does not move twice

  Scenario: AC9 The rules and timers are read from governed rows (new, D-RCV-60)
    When the step reads its rules and timers
    Then every rule ID, condition, timer and message text comes from a governed row with a version and none is written in code
